scope: Static source audit of the selected SolarCompositionModel.evaluate call path. No model execution, test rerun, thermal adequacy or physical-equivalence claim.
conclusion: The native Ca/Ly-alpha OTS path already shares the actual four-level Ca absorption between H destruction probability, albedo, electron-escape remainder and destroyed-photon allocation. The missing legacy Ca opacity in the C23 reference is not present on this audited path. No native change to match legacy C23 is indicated.

equations.photoelectron_heat_erg_cm3_s: Q_Ca = sum_i Phi_OTS n_i sigma_i [h nu_Lya - (IP_CaII - E_i)]

feedback: Actual state-dependent Ca II excited populations enter opacity, rather than the unused legacy Cloudy population variable.
Ca II->Ca III events enter the charge target; the same level loss enters excitation equilibrium.
Unpacked metal charges contribute to common electron density, and metal kinetic heat enters the thermal ledger.
Direct Fe/Ly-alpha line exchange is added outside generic continuum OTS, avoiding the independent legacy Fe allocation issue.
limits: The supplied Ca cross sections apply only to the Ly-alpha destruction/receiver prescription. They do not define a broadband excited-Ca photoionization continuum or complete inverse-Milne closure.
This source audit establishes the connected bookkeeping, not the numerical size or adequacy of the resulting atmospheric feedback.
The existing test checks conditional opacity, ionization and kinetic-energy consistency. It is not an atmosphere-level thermal or observational validation.

Ca opacity also enters the point-frequency stellar Ly-alpha attenuation used for H pumping; without a broadband cross-section law this does not establish a complete integrated stellar Ca absorption budget.
